conclusion: No live frame-internal scalar virtual value is destroyed in admitted production FMA frames; no allocator defect found

allocator.spill: CallOp spills every call-clobbered GPR local plus every dirty global
allocator.pinning: PinSelect observes HAS_CALLS and returns without pinning when has_call is true. Independently, its call-free pinnable pool explicitly excludes RSI/RDI as codegen_scratch. Thus no pinned RDI/RSI global can bypass the frame entry spill.

frame_closure.standalone: RvvEmitTypedFmaChunkGroup -> RvvEmitTypedFpChunkBody constructs VPR values only, state-relative loads/stores, VPR fbroadcast, masks/bracket; no scalar virtual definition or use
frame_closure.widening: RvvEmitTypedFWidenChunkGroup uses vector widening and the same vchunkfma; no scalar virtual live through classification
frame_closure.run: RvvEmitVectorRunGroup component SSA, f/x scalar broadcasts produce VPRs directly from CPUState; memory base offsets are state-backed, not allocated scalar virtuals; scalar guest instructions cut FormRun
frame_closure.scratch: RAX/RDX/RDI/RSI are emitter-internal temporaries; no temporary read at subsequent member boundary; VPR0 and kscr are reserved; kact preserved; 16-byte stack classification slots balanced
frame_closure.run_memory: InstVChunkLoad state-relative constructor supplies input0 as an I32 constant zero and uses base_state_offs/disp, rather than an address virtual GPR; the address-VOperand constructor is not used by production whole-load members. arch_traits.cpp assigns CT(vchunkload,r_ru32), so the zero constant remains an immediate; broadcasts use CT(...,r) with no scalar input operands.
